title: AffectOmni: RL-Verifiable People-Centric Grounded Affective Reasoning for Social and Art-Related Scenes
abstract: arXiv:2608.26193v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance on VQA and scene understanding, yet affective reasoning remains vulnerable to shortcut behavior. Models may predict correct answers while neglecting people-centric cues such as micro expressions and body language, which weakens traceability and external verification. Prior reinforcement learning approaches mainly reward context or logical coherence without explicitly enforcing attention to human evidence. In addition, LLM as a Judge scoring often suffers from score clustering, which reduces reward discriminability. We propose AffectOmni, a GRPO trained framework for verifiable affective reasoning. AffectOmni introduces People Focus and Temporal Order rewards to encourage people-centric evidence selection and temporally structured reasoning, and it adopts within-group comparative scoring to produce more stable and discriminative reward signals. translated_title: AffectOmni：面向社交与艺术场景的基于强化学习可验证的人物中心情感推理
translated_abstract: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在视觉问答和场景理解方面表现出色，但情感推理仍然容易受到捷径行为的影响。模型可能在忽略人物中心线索（如微表情和肢体语言）的情况下预测出正确答案，这削弱了可追溯性和外部验证性。先前的强化学习方法主要奖励上下文或逻辑连贯性，而没有明确强制模型关注人类证据。此外，作为评判者的LLM评分常常面临分数聚集问题，这降低了奖励的区分度。我们提出了AffectOmni，一个基于GRPO训练的框架，用于可验证的情感推理。AffectOmni引入了人物焦点和时间顺序奖励，以鼓励人物中心证据选择和时间结构化推理，并采用组内比较评分来产生更稳定且更具区分度的奖励信号。为进行验证，采用了一种思考（Thinkin）机制。
tldr: AffectOmni通过引入人物焦点和时间顺序奖励以及组内比较评分，解决了多模态大语言模型在情感推理中忽视人物线索和奖励区分度低的问题，实现了可验证的人物中心情感推理。
en_tdlr: AffectOmni addresses shortcut behavior in multimodal affective reasoning by introducing people-centric and temporal-order rewards with within-group comparative scoring, enabling verifiable and discriminative emotional inference.
